children: Themed ‘India in Motion’, the sixth edition will award 50 grants to artists, artisans and creative collectives, with applications open until 15 November 2026

Hyundai Motor India Foundation (HMIF), the corporate social responsibility (CSR) arm of Hyundai Motor India Limited, has announced the launch of the sixth season of its flagship Art for Hope initiative, offering grants worth Rs 60 lakh to support creative projects across India.

Themed ‘India in Motion’, Season 6 invites artists, artisans, collectives and creative practitioners to explore how a rapidly evolving India is shaping new ideas, identities and possibilities through art. Selected grantees will receive financial support, mentorship, national visibility and an opportunity to showcase their work at the Art for Hope Festival.

Applications are open across six categories: Visual Art, Digital Art, Performing Art, Traditional Art & Craft, Functional Art and Multidisciplinary Projects. The initiative will award 50 grants in this edition.
Building A Platform For Emerging Artists

Commenting on the launch of Art for Hope Season 6, Tarun Garg, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Hyundai Motor India Limited, says, “At Hyundai, our global vision of ‘Progress for Humanity’ goes beyond mobility to create opportunities that empower people and communities.

Through ‘Art for Hope’, we have awarded over INR 2.20 crore in grants, supported 200+ artists across India and helped preserve more than 75 traditional and folk-art forms. With Season 6 providing grants worth a total of INR 60 lakh, we look forward to enabling creative voices that reflect the aspirations, diversity and dynamism of a rapidly evolving Bharat. Guided by the virtues of Trust. Pride. Progress. we remain committed to fostering cultural inclusion, creativity and community development through art.”

Since its inception, Art for Hope has expanded its reach across 22 States and Union Territories, supporting more than 200 artists and awarding grants worth Rs 2.20 crore. The initiative has also promoted over 75 traditional and folk-art forms.

Its annual festivals have welcomed more than 35,000 visitors, including 61 per cent first-time exhibition visitors. The platform has also supported over 100 artisan and non-governmental organisation (NGO) stalls, helping generate livelihood opportunities and improve visibility for grassroots creative talent.
‘India In Motion’ Focuses On A Changing Nation

The Season 6 theme, ‘India in Motion’, reflects a nation shaped by changing communities, cultures, ideas and aspirations. It encourages artists to explore how progress, innovation and inclusion are influencing lives across urban and rural India.

The initiative will also continue its ‘Art without Barriers’ approach, encouraging participation from underserved and marginalised communities, including persons with disabilities. It aims to create opportunities for emerging creative voices, women, rural artisans and traditional and folk artists through financial assistance, mentorship and platforms to showcase their work.
